messages:
oncall-bot: AUTO-PAGE -> Emma SRE: Multiple high-latency alerts for model 'gptx-large' serving in region west-us-4 (gpu-scheduler errors). Severity: P2. Link: https://redwood.internal/alerts/1928001123

Emma SRE: I'm seeing p95 gen latency jump to ~3.2s and some 5xxs. Kube events show scheduler pod restarts on gpu-wus4-a pool. Scaling not recovering.

Jordan SRE: confirmed from metrics: scheduler queue depth spiked at 02:07 UTC, backlog growing for large-context requests. This looks like scheduler-side throttling not node-GPU OOMs.

Maya Ops: tagging customers in west-us-4 tenant groups who may hit errors. Should we do immediate regional reroute?

Emma SRE: yes, recommend routing all gptx-large traffic off west-us-4 to west-us-2 and west-us-3 while we triage. Low-cost immediate mitigation: update routing policy to zero weight for west-us-4 for that model.

Matt Eng: working on a quick root cause query, but agree on reroute first. I'll prepare the rollback/trace steps.

Emma SRE: executing reroute now. Command:```bash
# set fallback for gptx-large away from west-us-4
redwood routing update --model gptx-large --set-region-weight west-us-4=0 --fallback-regions west-us-2,west-us-3
```

oncall-bot: ACTION LOGGED -> Emma SRE ran routing update at 02:12 UTC (job id r-1928001123-3).

infra-bot: NOTE -> Traffic shift started. Observing 35% traffic to west-us-2, 65% to west-us-3 (weights applied). No errors from routing system.

Jordan SRE: early signals: p95 in west-us-4 dropping (less traffic) but overall p95 cluster-wide still elevated ~2.1s. Looks like queued requests draining.

Maya Ops: Draft status page update below. Please approve quick publish: 
"We are investigating elevated latencies and intermittent errors affecting large-model generation in West US (west-us-4). Mitigation: traffic for affected models is being routed to alternate regions (west-us-2, west-us-3). Impact: customers running large-context generation in west-us-4 may see increased latency or failures. We will post updates every 30 minutes."

Linda Product: approve. add 'no data loss' note and expected next update time.

Emma SRE: publishing now. Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1928001123 (published: Investigating -> Action in progress).

Matt Eng: FYI the scheduler controller logs show repeated backpressure decisions on long-running batches. Suspect a kernel/driver regression after yesterday's infra package bump. I'm collecting the exact log snippets.

Emma SRE: can we try a rolling restart of scheduler pods in that pool after traffic drained? That might restore normal scheduling behavior.

Jordan SRE: agreed. Will coordinate restart in 10m. Command we will use:```bash
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/gpu-scheduler-wus4-a --selector=pool=gpu-wus4-a
```

oncall-bot: SCHEDULE -> Jordan SRE scheduled restart at 02:25 UTC.

Raj Oncall: jumping in for the next handoff window (02:30-03:30). Emma, handoff to me once restart completes and we have stable metrics.

Emma SRE: handing off. Key facts in case: 1) cause likely scheduler backpressure after infra pkg update; 2) reroute applied at 02:12 UTC; 3) restart scheduled 02:25 UTC; 4) status page updated and customers notified.

Raj Oncall: ack. I'll monitor and escalate to infra eng if restarts don't clear the backlog by 02:40 UTC.

infra-bot: DEPLOYMENT -> Restart completed for deployment/gpu-scheduler-wus4-a at 02:26 UTC (rollout id r-1928001123-rr1).

Jordan SRE: post-restart checks: scheduler queue depth returning to baseline, new dispatching rate increased ~30%, p95 cluster-wide decreased to ~1.1s, west-us-4 errors dropping.

Emma SRE: rolling back the routing policy to allow west-us-4 back to normal weight. Command:```bash
redwood routing update --model gptx-large --set-region-weight west-us-4=0.45 --set-region-weight west-us-2=0.28 --set-region-weight west-us-3=0.27
```

oncall-bot: ACTION LOGGED -> Emma SRE ran routing update at 02:34 UTC (job id r-1928001123-4).

infra-bot: Traffic normalization complete by 02:37 UTC. No further 5xx trend.

Emma SRE: status page follow-up draft: "Mitigation completed: scheduling service in west-us-4 was restarted and traffic was shifted back. We continue to monitor. Root cause under investigation; initial hypothesis points to an infra package regression that increases scheduler backpressure on long batches. No customer data loss detected."

Linda Product: please send a short customer notification for affected tenants. Suggested template below.

Maya Ops: customer notification template: 
"Hello — we experienced degraded performance for large-model generation in West US (west-us-4) on <date/time>. We routed traffic to alternate regions and restarted the scheduler in west-us-4; service is now returning to normal. We are investigating the root cause and will follow up with a technical postmortem. No data loss occurred. If you saw errors or need help validating your workloads, reply and we'll assist."

Raj Oncall: I'll keep the channel open for 1h monitoring. If anything regresses, I'll re-escalate and page infra-eng. Otherwise, planning to transition incident to postmortem at 06:00 UTC.

Emma SRE: thanks team. Quick follow-ups for postmortem: collect scheduler logs (02:00-02:30), infra pkg diff from yesterday's roll, and routing audit entries. Assigning owners: Matt Eng (pkg diff & repro), Jordan SRE (logs & metrics), Linda Product (customer comms).

Matt Eng: ack. I'll start a PR to pin package and run a canary in west-us-3.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT -> set severity P2 -> assigned to Emma SRE, transitions: triage -> mitigated -> monitoring.

Emma SRE: closing thread for active mitigation handoff to Raj. Keeping notes pinned in the incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1928001123/notes

Raj Oncall: watching. ping me if you need a re-page. :thumbsup:
